h: Ogres, Donkeys and a Day on the South Bank
p: County Hall is one of the grandest buildings on the South Bank, a former seat of London's government that now houses a mix of hotels, restaurants and family attractions. Its address on Westminster Bridge Road puts you right in the thick of it, with the river on one side and Waterloo on the other. It's about as central as days out get.

Shrek's Adventure is very much one for families, so it helps to think about who's coming. Younger children who know the films inside out tend to get the most from it, but older kids and grown-up fans can find plenty to laugh at too, thanks to the cheeky humour and live performances. Some scenes are dark and a little spooky, so if you've got a very nervous little one, it's worth bearing in mind.

A few practical tips. Arrive a little before your slot so you're not rushing, and use the toilets first, as you'll be moving through the experience with your group. Pushchairs and bags can be awkward in the themed rooms, so travel light if you can. And because it's all indoors, it's a reliable choice on a wet London day.

If you're making a day of it, the South Bank has loads more to offer. Jubilee Gardens is a handy open space for little ones to run around, and the Southbank Centre often has free events and installations along the river. Further along, the Tate Modern and the Millennium Bridge are a pleasant walk east, and Gabriel's Wharf has little shops and places to eat. Westminster Abbey is just across the river if you fancy a bit of history.
